client_situation.text: The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC) is the issuing body, and the study is performed for MHTC and the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), with MoDOT's Right of Way staff reviewing drafts.
The work is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, and the Offeror must fully coordinate its activities with that division.
MoDOT's Right of Way staff must produce property descriptions that accurately define the land areas or rights acquired, conveyed or leased, reciting specific rights when less than fee simple title.

Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet the requirements of MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2.

Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to the grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify the parcel matches the right of way plans and that those plans match the surveyor's survey information.
Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the research.

The business driver is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for producing a "first draft" legal land description (LLD) from MHTC parameters that MoDOT Right of Way staff could review and edit.

goal.text: The client wants a research study, TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions," that determines whether AI/ML can generate a first draft of a legal land description using MHTC parameters for review and editing by MoDOT Right of Way staff.
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the final invoice due and contract ending February 2, 2026.
Task 2 requires a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.
Task 3b requires the Offeror to name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.

Task 3c requires a proof-of-concept demonstration of how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving improvement feedback.
Task 4 requires the Offeror to train ROW staff on the finalized system and supply a user manual for staff reference.

Task 5 requires a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary plus supporting documentation, and Task 6 requires a final report with all findings, a 1-2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff.
Task 1 requires a kick-off meeting, quarterly project status meetings with minutes, and a Data Management Plan submitted within 2 weeks after kick-off.

success_criteria.text: Proposals are due by email to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.

All questions and comments must go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by July 17, 2024 at 4 p.m. Central, and contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its responses to questions publicly on July 31, 2024, and notifies submitters about project selection or interviews on September 18, 2024.

After a responsiveness check, proposals are evaluated against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee, and the award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal; the RFP does not list the specific criteria or weights.

The Work Plan must be narrative, limited to ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points (excluding attached forms and resumes), must cover all items in Section 2, and must recognize MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.

Proposals must be one combined PDF in a fixed order: Proposal Submission Form, optional one-page cover letter, body of proposal (work plan and schedule), Personnel, Organization's Project Experience, Team Member Experience, and Organization's Client References.

The proposal must identify experience in offering the requested services during the past three years and give at least three client references with name, title and telephone number from the past three years.

The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs on April 25, 2025 for MoDOT feedback, deliver the manual and ROW training by July 25, 2025, complete the interim presentation by September 15, 2025, and deliver the draft final report, summary and user manual by November 3, 2025.

constraints.text: Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, and the cost estimate must be entered on the Section (4) Price Page with line items for Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost, Miscellaneous and Total.

Applications must be built on approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or a currently supported .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed), with web applications using MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, and approved languages limited to C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, with Python reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves larger use.

Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management.

Applications must be web-based browser applications requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets, no Silverlight), must run on Oracle 19C or a supported SQL Server version, and must meet WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard.
No Personal Identifiable Information (PII) may be stored in any database table without a specific business need, and all stored PII requires approval from the IS Cyber Security Team.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and the Offeror must keep working papers available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor for three years after final payment.
The Data Management Plan must describe anticipated data formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used to ensure maximum future utility of the data.

Award is subject to a post-award negotiated contract that MHTC may cancel if terms cannot be agreed, and the RFP requires 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation targets, an E-Verify affidavit (Exhibit A), lawful-presence affidavits for sole proprietorships and partnerships (Exhibit B), and insurance of $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence for general and automobile liability plus Missouri workers' compensation.

solution.summary: The bid is a 15-month research and development engagement, not a software procurement: we deliver a proof-of-concept AI/ML tool that drafts legal land descriptions from MHTC parameters, together with the evidence, training and reporting that let MoDOT decide whether the technology is useful. The work runs in six phases — kick-off and planning, literature and peer-state review, program selection and MoDOT IS approval, proof-of-concept build and demonstration, training and manual, then synthesis and final reporting — each gated by a MoDOT review point. We build the prototype on the approved MoDOT technology stack (.NET 6.0 or above, MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, C#/JavaScript/HTML/CSS, Python only for ESRI scripts or small one-time uses) and host it in a MoDOT-approved environment, with no third-party licensing burden placed on MoDOT. The team is a small, senior one: a principal investigator and land-surveying subject-matter expert, an AI/ML engineer, a .NET developer, a technical writer/trainer and a part-time contract and compliance lead, with a professional land surveyor reviewing every generated description. Everything is priced to the $175,000 not-to-exceed ceiling on the Section (4) Price Page, and all deliverables, data and working papers remain MHTC property. A bid-administration workstream owns the RFP's own calendar — the question deadline, the proposal deadline and the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window for every RFP event — so the offer is submitted on time and through the single permitted channel.

Questions and comments go only to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by the date and time in Section 1E (17 July 2024, 4 p.m. Central), with no contact with MoDOT employees by any other method; the proposal is emailed to the same address by 21 August 2024, 10 a.m. Central, and we treat submission as complete only when MoDOT's notification of receipt arrives. Every RFP event we schedule or attend — question submission, proposal delivery, any interview or clarification session — is booked inside the 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central window, and the calendar is tracked against a written submission checklist with a time buffer before each deadline. The same workstream assembles the single combined PDF in the required order and confirms the Proposal Submission Form, signatures and contact details are present.

components.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
components.description: A named project manager runs the engagement under a finalized work plan that details every task, resource and schedule commitment and explicitly recognizes MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. We facilitate the kick-off meeting to confirm scope, schedule and a communications protocol, then hold quarterly status meetings (in person or online) with written minutes for the kick-off and every quarterly meeting, submit quarterly progress updates by the last working day of March, June, September and December, and maintain monthly email and phone updates to MoDOT contacts. All activity is coordinated with the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, and advice and information on Agreement matters is available to that Division throughout the term. A single MHTC representative channel handles concerns about administration of the services.

claims.text: The contract period is 15 months, with an estimated 1 November 2024 start and a final invoice and contract end date of 2 February 2026.
The work is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, with which the Offeror must fully coordinate.

components.title: Data Management Plan and research data handling
components.description: Within two weeks of kick-off we submit a Data Management Plan that names the anticipated formats for every data type the study produces — source deeds and right-of-way plans, MHTC parameter sets, training corpora, model artefacts, generated descriptions and review comments — and commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats (plain text, CSV, PDF/A, GeoJSON where spatial) so the data retains maximum future utility for MoDOT. The plan also states retention, access and handover arrangements consistent with MHTC ownership of all data and deliverables and with records being available to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor for three years after final payment. No PII is stored in any database table without a documented business need and IS Cyber Security Team approval.

claims.text: The Data Management Plan is due within two weeks after the kick-off meeting.

components.title: Literature search and peer-state practice review
components.description: A structured review of published research and of other state DOTs' use of AI/ML for right-of-way work, covering document-drafting and deed-description automation, spatial data extraction, and the accuracy, liability and professional-surveyor review questions those uses raise. We deliver an annotated bibliography, a comparison matrix of peer-state practice and a findings memo that feeds directly into the program selection and the proof-of-concept design, so the demonstration is grounded in what has already been shown to work rather than starting from zero.

claims.text: Task 2 requires a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes.

components.title: Program selection and MoDOT Information Systems approval
components.description: We name the specific program used to develop the LLDs before any proof-of-concept work begins, and submit it to MoDOT Information Systems with the information that review needs: version, licensing model, hosting location, data flows, security posture and any third-party dependencies. We do not proceed to the proof-of-concept demonstration until MoDOT IS has approved the named program, and we hold a schedule contingency for that approval. The selection is constrained to the approved technology stack — .NET 6.0 or above (or a supported .NET Framework 4.8+ where specifically needed), MVC/Razor Pages/Web API, C#/JavaScript/HTML/CSS, with Python limited to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the IS Best Practices Review Team approves more — and to components that place no licensing responsibility on MoDOT without BRPT and IS management approval.

claims.text: Task 3b requires the Offeror to name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c proceeds.

components.title: Legal land description rules engine and drafting prototype
components.description: The core build: a rules-and-template layer that encodes MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 requirements and the MHTC drafting conventions, so that generated descriptions use metes and bounds for partial acquisitions, reproduce the last deed of record verbatim where a property is acquired in its entirety, and recite the specific rights acquired, conveyed or leased whenever the interest is less than fee simple. The AI/ML component drafts from MHTC parameters supplied per property and produces a clearly marked first draft for Right of Way staff to review and edit, with every generated call and bearing traceable to its source input. The application is a browser-based web application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, tested against the latest IS-approved browsers, meeting WCAG 2.1 AA and the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard, running on Oracle 19C or an approved SQL Server version, and free of vendor branding where a licensed option removes it and of unlicensed third-party content.

claims.text: Realty rights acquired or conveyed by MHTC must be described by metes and bounds unless the property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Descriptions prepared for MHTC must meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2.

components.title: Proof-of-concept demonstration and surveyor verification
components.description: A live demonstration on 25 April 2025 in which the technology generates draft legal land descriptions across a spread of property types — partial takes, whole-parcel acquisitions, easements and less-than-fee interests — with MoDOT Right of Way staff reviewing the drafts and giving structured improvement feedback that we log, triage and fold into the next iteration. Each generated description is checked by a professional land surveyor against the right-of-way plans and the surveyor's survey information before it is presented as a candidate for deed use, mirroring the review MoDOT requires before a deed reaches a grantor. We report measured accuracy and staff editing effort per property so MoDOT can judge usefulness, not just feasibility.

claims.text: The Offeror must present how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs on 25 April 2025 for MoDOT feedback.
Before a deed is presented to a grantor, a professional land surveyor must verify the description matches the right-of-way plans and the survey information.

components.title: Training, user manual and knowledge transfer
components.description: Once the system is finalized we train Right of Way staff and deliver a user manual for ongoing reference, both by 25 July 2025. Training is role-based — drafters, reviewers and approvers — covering parameter entry, reading and correcting a generated description, the surveyor verification step and the audit trail, delivered in sessions plus recorded walkthroughs so staff can revisit them. The manual is delivered electronically and in print-ready form, covering installation and access, every workflow, the EPG 236.4.6.2 rules the tool applies, troubleshooting and worked examples, and is updated to match the final system at project close.

claims.text: The manual and ROW training must be delivered by 25 July 2025.

components.title: Synthesis, final reporting and research summary
components.description: A draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary with supporting documentation, delivered by 3 November 2025, followed by the final report containing all findings, a 1–2 page research summary stating objectives, findings and conclusions, and a presentation for MoDOT staff. The final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page and follows the Publications Guidelines and summary template. The synthesis answers the research question directly: whether AI/ML can usefully produce a first draft LLD from MHTC parameters, under what conditions, with what review burden and what residual risk — and recommends next steps for MoDOT adoption.

claims.text: The draft final report, summary and user manual are due by 3 November 2025.

It also carries the employment and insurance package: E-Verify MOU, the sworn affidavit of no unauthorized-alien employment, lawful-presence affidavits for sole proprietors and general partners, general and automobile liability at $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Missouri workers' compensation, and certificates of insurance available on request. We commit to 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation and to direct hiring of minorities and women.

The RFP requires 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation targets, an E-Verify affidavit, lawful-presence affidavits, and insurance of $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence plus Missouri workers' compensation.

claims.text: Services are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000, with the cost estimate entered on the Section (4) Price Page.

assumptions.text: The MHTC parameters are assumed to be the right-of-way plan data, parcel and ownership records, deed references and acquisition instructions that MoDOT Right of Way staff currently use to hand-write descriptions; we will confirm the exact parameter set at kick-off and treat it as a fixed input specification for the prototype.

MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2 is assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT's public Engineering Policy Guide and to be stable for the project term; we will encode it as a versioned ruleset and re-verify it at each review gate rather than assume it is supplied with the RFP.

The 1 November 2024 start is assumed to be the planning baseline, with the 2 February 2026 contract end and the fixed milestone dates (25 April 2025 demonstration, 25 July 2025 training and manual, 15 September 2025 interim presentation, 3 November 2025 draft deliverables) treated as binding and not re-opened at kick-off.
The interim presentation is assumed to fall at the September 2025 milestone already named in the schedule, which we treat as the project mid-point.

The proof-of-concept is assumed to cover a representative sample of roughly ten to fifteen properties spanning partial takes, whole-parcel acquisitions, easements and less-than-fee interests, sized to fit within the $175,000 ceiling; the exact count will be agreed with MoDOT at kick-off.

Training is assumed to be delivered as a small number of virtual or on-site sessions for the Right of Way staff who will use the tool, plus recorded walkthroughs and one electronic and print-ready manual, rather than repeated sessions for the whole division.

The prototype is assumed to be hosted in a MoDOT-approved environment on Oracle 19C, with SQL Server used only if MoDOT IS approves it, and no PII stored, since the study works from property and deed data rather than personal records.

The named LLD development program is assumed to be a commercially or openly licensed tool whose licence sits with the Offeror or is otherwise free of cost and licensing responsibility for MoDOT, so that BRPT review is a confirmation step rather than a procurement.

The literature review is assumed to be delivered as an annotated bibliography plus a peer-state comparison memo and a short briefing at a quarterly meeting, covering the past ten years of US state DOT practice, rather than a standalone published report.

The cost estimate is assumed to be a total-contract-value estimate for the full 15-month period of performance, detailed by labour category, hours and rates, since a detailed budget is developed only after award.
The 10% MBE and 5% WBE targets are assumed to be measured against total contract value and reported in the proposal with named subcontracting partners, even though the RFP states them as encouraged.
The insurance limits are assumed to be binding at contract signing, with certificates of insurance provided on request before award.
Confidential MHTC material is assumed to be identified by marking at the time it is supplied, and we will notify MHTC's representative within one business day of any third-party request for it.

The Offeror is assumed to retain ownership of its pre-existing models, code and tooling, granting MHTC the royalty-free right to reproduce and use products derived from the work, with all study deliverables and MHTC-supplied information remaining MHTC property.

The question deadline is assumed to be 17 July 2024 at 4 p.m. Central, the date carried on the contact row of the RFP timetable, and the proposal deadline is assumed to be fixed at 21 August 2024 at 10 a.m. Central even though MoDOT reserves the right to expand the rest of the schedule.

risks.title: Fixed milestone dates may be re-opened at kick-off, leaving the 25 April 2025 demonstration and 25 July 2025 training unachievable
risks.description: The RFP fixes a 25 April 2025 demonstration, 25 July 2025 training and manual, a September 2025 interim presentation and 3 November 2025 draft deliverables, yet the same table says milestone dates will be determined at the kick-off meeting and the schedule is only an estimate presuming a 1 November 2024 start. If the start slips or the dates move, the six-phase plan compresses and the demonstration, training and reporting dates are missed. Missing a contractual date on a research contract of this size is a material failure for the bidder and delays MoDOT's decision on the technology.
risks.justification: The RFP both fixes and unfixes the same dates, and the schedule is explicitly an estimate pending contracting, so a later start is plausible; the consequence is a missed contractual milestone.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal that the milestone dates in the RFP table are treated as binding and that any later start is handled by a written schedule amendment, and ask MoDOT before the deadline whether the 1 November 2024 start and the listed milestone dates are fixed.

risks.title: MoDOT IS approval of the named LLD program gates the proof of concept
risks.description: The RFP requires the Offeror to name the program used to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins and requires MoDOT Information Systems to approve it before the demonstration phase may proceed. The RFP does not say what information must accompany the name or what criteria and turnaround the approval uses. If approval is slow or the chosen program is rejected, the 25 April 2025 demonstration slips and the bidder carries unplanned idle effort inside a fixed ceiling.
risks.justification: The approval is a hard gate on the critical path to a fixed demonstration date, and the RFP leaves both the submission content and the approval timeline open.
risks.mitigation: Name the program in the proposal with version, licensing model, hosting location, data flows and security posture, ask MoDOT IS before the deadline what else it needs and how long review takes, and hold explicit schedule contingency between approval and the demonstration.

risks.title: The $175,000 ceiling may not cover a surveyor-verified prototype plus training and reporting
risks.description: The RFP caps the work at a not-to-exceed $175,000 for a 15-month engagement that includes a literature review, a program approval cycle, a working AI/ML prototype, a professional land surveyor reviewing every generated description, role-based training, a user manual and a final report. The proposed solution prices a five-person senior team to that ceiling and assumes a sample of roughly ten to fifteen properties. If the property sample, training volume or surveyor review effort is larger than assumed, the bidder absorbs the overrun or cuts scope that MoDOT expects.
risks.justification: The ceiling is fixed and the RFP leaves the demonstration sample, training volume and manual scope undefined, so the effort that drives cost is not settled; a senior team plus surveyor review is expensive relative to the cap.
risks.mitigation: State the assumed property count, training session count and manual scope explicitly in the proposal as the basis of the price, and ask MoDOT before the deadline to confirm the expected demonstration sample and training volume.

risks.title: MHTC parameters and EPG Section 236.4.6.2 are not defined or supplied
risks.description: The RFP requires the tool to draft from 'MHTC parameters' and to meet MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, but neither the parameter set nor the EPG section is included. The proposed solution assumes the parameters are right-of-way plan data, parcel and ownership records and deed references, and that the EPG section is publicly available and stable. If the real parameter set is different or the EPG rules are more intricate than assumed, the rules engine and the drafting model are rebuilt after kick-off, inside a fixed ceiling and a fixed demonstration date.
risks.justification: The core technical input and the governing drafting standard are both undefined in the RFP, and the solution's reading of them is an explicit inference rather than a confirmed fact.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT before the deadline for a sample MHTC parameter set and confirmation of which EPG 236.4.6.2 version governs, and state in the proposal that the parameter specification is fixed at kick-off and that changes to it are handled by written amendment.

risks.title: Contract term of 15 months conflicts with a 2 February 2026 end date
risks.description: The RFP states a 15-month contract period and separately ends the contract on 2 February 2026, which is roughly 14.5 months after the estimated 1 November 2024 start. The proposed solution prices and staffs a full 15 months and treats both as binding. If the shorter period governs, the final reporting phase and the last quarterly update fall outside the term and the bidder either absorbs unbilled effort or negotiates a change order.
risks.justification: The two statements cannot both be true from the same start date, and the RFP does not say which governs; the gap is about two weeks of effort, absorbable but real.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT to confirm whether the term is 15 months from the actual start or ends on 2 February 2026, and build the cost estimate on the shorter of the two with the final report scheduled before the end date.

risks.title: Oracle 19C and SQL Server requirements point at incompatible database platforms
risks.description: One requirement mandates Oracle 19C for on-premise deployments while another directs the application to be designed and maintained on the latest supported SQL Server, with SQL Server 2016 or higher only if MoDOT IS approves. The proposed solution hedges by saying it runs on Oracle 19C or an approved SQL Server version. If the platform is not settled before the build, the prototype's data layer is built twice or rebuilt late, and the proof-of-concept demonstration date is at risk.
risks.justification: The two requirements are directly contradictory and the RFP does not say whether they are alternatives or whether Oracle is the default; the prototype is small, so rework is material but not fatal.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT IS before the deadline which platform the prototype must run on and what approval SQL Server needs, and design the data access layer so the database can be swapped without rewriting the rules engine.

risks.title: Licensing and Python approval gates could force a redesign of the prototype
risks.description: The RFP bars third-party tools that place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior BRPT and IS management approval, and reserves Python for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless the BRPT approves larger use. The proposed solution assumes the named program's licence sits with the Offeror at no cost to MoDOT and that Python use stays small. If either assumption is wrong, the bidder must re-select the program or rewrite components in C#, and the approval queue adds weeks to a fixed schedule.
risks.justification: The solution's own assumptions make both approvals confirmation steps, but the RFP sets no threshold for 'large scale' Python and no criteria for the licensing review, so rejection is plausible.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal that the named program's licence is held by the Offeror with no cost or licensing obligation for MoDOT, keep Python to ESRI scripts only, and ask the BRPT before the deadline what it treats as large-scale Python use.

risks.title: Exhibits A and B are referenced but not in the RFP
risks.description: The RFP requires an E-Verify MOU, a sworn affidavit of no unauthorized-alien employment and lawful-presence affidavits for sole proprietors and general partners, and points to Exhibit A and Exhibit B for the forms, but neither exhibit is in the document. The proposed solution commits to the affidavits without having seen the forms. If the forms cannot be obtained or require information the bidder does not hold at submission, the proposal is incomplete and can be disqualified.
risks.justification: The obligation is mandatory and the forms are missing from the RFP, so the bidder cannot confirm it can complete them correctly before the deadline.
risks.mitigation: Request Exhibit A and Exhibit B from MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov before the question deadline, and prepare the E-Verify MOU and affidavits in draft so they can be signed as soon as the forms arrive.

risks.title: Unreadable pages 19 and 20 may carry requirements the proposal does not answer
risks.description: Pages 19 and 20 of the RFP could not be read: each has only 19 words of text and an image covering more than half the page. Those pages sit in the section that sets out the kick-off, Data Management Plan and task requirements. If they contain task detail, deliverable formats or review gates, the proposal may be non-responsive on a mandatory item without the bidder knowing.
risks.justification: The pages fall in a substantive part of the scope of work and the text is largely unreadable, so a missed requirement is plausible; the consequence is a responsiveness failure rather than a delivery failure.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT for a text-searchable copy of pages 19 and 20 before the question deadline, and cross-check the work plan and Data Management Plan against whatever those pages contain before submission.

risks.title: The Price Page form is not provided, so the cost estimate may not match the required format
risks.description: The RFP requires the fee proposal on the Section (4) Price Page with Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, F&A, Miscellaneous and Total, but the form itself is not in the document. The proposed solution builds a bottom-up estimate and maps it to those categories. If the actual form has different line items, a different period basis or a prescribed breakdown, the estimate must be rebuilt close to the deadline and may not be comparable to other offers.
risks.justification: The pricing form is mandatory and missing, and the RFP also leaves open whether the estimate covers the total contract value or an annual basis.
risks.mitigation: Obtain the Price Page from the MoDOT information-for-researchers page or by question before the deadline, and prepare the estimate so it can be re-cut into any prescribed line-item structure without re-pricing.

risks.title: Evaluation criteria and weights are not disclosed
risks.description: The RFP says proposals are evaluated against criteria set by the Technical Advisory Committee but does not list the criteria or their weights, and states that MHTC is not obliged to solicit missing information. The proposed solution allocates effort across a ten-page work plan, personnel, experience and references without knowing what is scored. If the weighting favours, for example, prior AI/ML or Missouri state-agency experience, the bid may be structured against the wrong strengths.
risks.justification: The criteria are absent from the RFP and the proposal is judged as submitted, so a misallocated emphasis directly affects the chance of award.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT before the deadline whether the evaluation criteria and weights can be shared, and structure the ten-page work plan so each Section 2 item and each differentiator is visible within the page limit.

risks.title: Post-award negotiated contract lets MHTC cancel the award
risks.description: The RFP makes award subject to a post-award negotiated contract and allows MHTC to cancel and select another Offeror if terms cannot be agreed, while the contract provisions themselves are not reproduced in the RFP. The proposed solution accepts the negotiated contract and its provisions. If the negotiated terms add obligations the bidder has not priced, such as broader IP rights or different insurance, the bidder either accepts an uneconomic contract or loses the award after spending bid effort.
risks.justification: Cancellation requires a negotiation breakdown, which is unusual, but the contract terms are not visible in the RFP and the bidder cannot price against them.
risks.mitigation: Review the Standard Research Agreement on the MoDOT website before submission, ask before the deadline which provisions are non-negotiable, and state in the proposal the assumptions on IP ownership and insurance on which the price rests.
